items.title: Equivariant constructible derived category of complex varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) carrying an algebraic action of a product $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ of complex general linear groups ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]). Form the analytic action nerve $G^p\times X$: the simplicial space whose $p$-th space is $G^p\times X$ with the usual face and degeneracy structure maps. In the abelian category of all simplicial sheaves of $k$-vector spaces on this nerve ([[def-sheaf-on-topological-space]], [[def-module-on-ringed-space]]), take its bounded derived category ([[def-derived-category-of-an-abelian-category]]). The full subcategory $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ consists of the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are Cartesian under every nerve structure map and whose restrictions to the degree-zero space $X$ are algebraically constructible with finite-dimensional stalks ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]). Boundedness means uniform cohomological boundedness in the simplicial sheaf category. Morphisms are morphisms in that ambient derived category, not morphisms in the derived category of naive equivariant sheaves. Set $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])$ with the ordinary cochain shift. Restriction to $X$ is the forgetful functor. The ambient category and its explicit coinduced injective resolutions are supplied by [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]; triangulatedness, local smallness, conservative restriction and the finite GL Stiefel resolution comparisons are established by [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], recorded as this definition's well-definedness discharge.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §2.1.1-2.1.7 (resolutions $p:P\to X$ and the categories $D^b(X,P)$), §2.2.1-2.2.5 (the limit definition of $D^b_G(X)$), §2.4.1-2.4.6 (the fibered-category description), §2.8 (constructible objects) and Appendix B1-B3 (the simplicial description: simplicial sheaves on $[G\backslash X]_\bullet$, the subcategory with isomorphism structure maps, and its bounded derived category); BBD §1.4.3 and §2.1.1-2.1.3 for the ordinary t-structure language. Step 1 (ambient category). The abelian category of all simplicial $k$-sheaves on the action nerve and its explicit coinduced injective resolutions are constructed by [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]], with bounded-below injective models from [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]. Step 2 (the full subcategory). Cartesian cohomology is the condition that every nerve structure map is an isomorphism on cohomology; degree-zero algebraic constructibility is read through [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and the shift convention is ordinary cohomological shift in the ambient derived category. Step 3 (well-definedness). Triangulatedness, local smallness, conservative restriction to $X$, idempotent completeness and the finite GL Stiefel resolution comparisons are the content of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]], recorded in justified_by rather than as a dependency edge because that lemma depends on this definition. This is a definition: no mathematical claim beyond well-formedness is made, and AC is inherited from the two construction suppliers.

items.title: Acyclic product fibers stabilize bounded constructible pullback Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $f:Y\to S$ be a locally trivial bundle in the finite constructible local-product setting of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]], with nonempty connected finite-type smooth fiber $F$. Suppose the constant-sheaf cohomology of the fiber is $k$ in degree zero and vanishes in degrees $1,\dots,r$. For $B\in D_c^{\ge b}(S;k)$ the cone of the unit $B\to Rf_*f^*B$ belongs to $D^{\ge b+r+1}$. For $A\in D_c^{\le a}$, pullback gives an isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A,f^*B[m])$ whenever $m\le b+r-a$. It is fully faithful on $D_c^{[b,a]}$ when $r\ge a-b$, and its image is characterized by the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ being an isomorphism and is closed under direct summands. Extension closure is asserted only for the stronger bound $r\ge a-b+1$; at $r=a-b$ only the degree-zero Hom comparison and retract closure are claimed. No global tensor splitting $Rf_*f^*B\simeq B\otimes R\Gamma(F;k)$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: reduce the unit-cone bound to the finite local product cochain comparison, glue it by local vanishing, and derive the Hom comparison and image description from the bounded t-structure. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §1.9.1-1.9.4 (definition of an $n$-acyclic map; the interval characterization of the image of $f^*$; the criterion for an object of $D^I(X)$ to come from the base; the Vietoris-Begle criterion) and Appendix A2-A4 (the proofs), together with §2.2.1-2.2.4 (limit over resolutions and the interval equivalence). Step 1 (local cone bound): for algebraically constructible $B$ choose a common finite conical triangulation of a product chart of $S$ and a finite CW model of $F$; the ordinary constructible sheaf/cochain comparison of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] identifies $Rf_*f^*B$ locally with the tensor product of the local cochain model of $B$ with $C^*(F;k)$, taking the unit to $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$; the cone of $k\to C^*(F;k)$ has cohomology in degrees $\ge r+1$, so tensoring with $B^{\ge b}$ gives $C^{\ge b+r+1}$, and cohomological vanishing is local ([[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] supplies the compatible finite models and their coefficient-field compatibility). Step 2 (Hom comparison): in the triangle $B\to Rf_*f^*B\to C$ with $C\ge b+r+1$, the long exact Hom sequence and the derived adjunction $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ of [[lem-bounded-analytic-field-sheaves-have-derived-tensor-hom-and-pullback-pushforward-adjunctions]] give the displayed isomorphism for $m\le b+r-a$, because $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(A,C[m-1])$ vanish by [[def-canonical-t-structure-on-a-derived-category]] orthogonality ([[thm-inverse-direct-image-adjunction]] is the underlying sheaf adjunction, and the ambient derived model is [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]]). Step 3 (image and closure): for an interval $I=[b,a]$ the counit $f^*\tau^{\le a}Rf_*C\to C$ exhibits $C$ as a pullback precisely when it is an isomorphism; this characterizes the image and proves closure under direct summands. If $r\ge a-b+1$ the degree-one comparison also lifts the connecting morphism of an extension, proving extension closure; at $r=a-b$ that lift is unavailable and is deliberately not used. No global tensor splitting is asserted: the comparison is local and characteristic-class transgressions are allowed. The statement keeps the corrected retract/extension boundary at $r=a-b$ exactly as the owner correction requires.

items.title: General linear frame spaces have the Stiefel cohomology gap
items.statement: Assume AC. For $n_i\ge1$, $N_i\ge n_i+1$ and a field $k$, put $U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i})$ and $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Each $\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^n,\mathbb C^N)$ is homotopy equivalent to the Stiefel space $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$; each $V_n(\mathbb C^N)$ is a compact path-connected smooth manifold homeomorphic to a finite CW complex, and the forgetting map $V_n(\mathbb C^N)\to V_{n-1}(\mathbb C^N)$ is a numerable locally trivial bundle with fiber $S^{2(N-n)+1}$, hence a Serre fibration. Consequently $H^0(U_N;k)\cong k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: retract the full-rank frame space onto the Stiefel manifold by Gram-Schmidt, verify the sphere-bundle structure of the forgetting map, and run the cohomological Serre spectral sequence on finite CW models. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, 3.1 (the Stiefel manifold of frames is an n-acyclic free manifold); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology Section 4.2 pp. 375-378 (Theorem 4.41) and the standard sphere-bundle induction computing the cohomology of the complex Stiefel manifolds. Step 1 (retraction): the QR factorization of a full-rank matrix is continuous with positive diagonal triangular factor, and contracting that factor to the identity deforms $\operatorname{Inj}$ onto $V_n$. Step 2 (manifold and CW model): $V_n$ is the regular level set $A^*A=I$ of a submersion on the full-rank locus, hence a compact smooth manifold, and the finite triangulation theorem and finite polyhedra give finite CW models. Step 3 (fibration): the forgetting map is locally trivial with sphere fiber and numerable over the compact base, hence a Serre fibration, and the base is path-connected by induction. Step 4 (spectral sequence): in total degrees at most $2(N-n)$ the only nonzero $E_2$ terms have fiber degree zero, so the induction on $n$ gives the stated gap; iterating the trivial product fibrations gives the product bound $r_N$.

references.locator: Section 4.2 pp. 375-378 (fiber bundles over paracompact bases are fibrations, Theorem 4.41); the cohomology of the complex Stiefel manifolds in the standard sphere-bundle induction; Example 0.6 and Section 3.2 (cells and cohomology of the spheres)

items.title: General linear Stiefel approximations stabilize bounded constructible Hom
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$ be a finite product of complex
general linear groups with $n_i\ge1$
([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]), acting algebraically on a
separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]],
[[def-algebraic-group-action-and-scheme-theoretic-stabilizer]]). For integers
$N_i\ge n_i+1$ put
$$U_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Inj}(\mathbb C^{n_i},\mathbb C^{N_i}),\qquad B_N=\prod_i\operatorname{Gr}(n_i,N_i),\qquad X_N=(U_N\times X)/G,$$
where $G$ acts on $U_N$ by precomposition of frames and on $U_N\times X$
diagonally, and set $r_N=2\min_i(N_i-n_i)$. Let
$p_N:G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$, with
$P_N=U_N\times X$ and $p_N=(\mathrm{id},\operatorname{pr}_X)$, be the
simplicial map of the two action nerves
([[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]]),
and let $Q_N:D^b_{G,c}(X;k)\to D_c^b(X_N;k)$ be the composite of $p_N^*$ with
the locally split Čech descent equivalence for the principal bundle
$P_N\to X_N$
([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]).
Then, for bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$:

1. **Hom comparison.** If $A\in D_c^{\le a}$ and $B\in D_c^{\ge b}$, then
   pullback induces an isomorphism
   $\operatorname{Hom}_G(A,B[m])\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X_N}(Q_N(A),Q_N(B)[m])$
   whenever $m\le b+r_N-a$;
2. **full faithfulness.** On an ordinary cohomological interval
   $D_c^{[b,a]}$ of width $a-b\le r_N$, the functor $Q_N$ is fully faithful;
3. **image.** On such an interval the image of $Q_N$ consists exactly of the
   objects $H$ whose principal-bundle pullback $q_N^*H$ lies in the image of
   $\operatorname{pr}_X^*:D_c^{[b,a]}(X;k)\to D_c^{[b,a]}(P_N;k)$, i.e. of
   the resolution triples whose frame-bundle pullback comes from $X$; the
   image is closed under retracts, and under extensions when
   $r_N\ge a-b+1$;
4. **coherence.** For two resolutions $N,M$, use the common product resolution
   $U_N\times U_M$ and its associated quotient
   $X_{N,M}=(U_N\times U_M\times X)/G$ with projections
   $\pi_N:X_{N,M}\to X_N$ and $\pi_M:X_{N,M}\to X_M$.
   The pullbacks $\pi_N^*Q_N(A)$ and $\pi_M^*Q_M(A)$ are canonically
   identified on intervals of width at most $\min(r_N,r_M)$, and their
   Hom comparisons commute with natural transformations and satisfy the
   cocycle identity after pullback to a triple product resolution.
   No identification of $U_N\times U_M$ with $U_{N+M}$ or direct
   isomorphism of functors with different target categories is asserted;
5. **trivial group.** If $G$ is trivial then $U_N$, $B_N$ and $X_N$ are $X$
   or a point, $r_N=\infty$, and $Q_N$ is the identity of $D_c^b(X;k)$.

No global tensor splitting
$Ra_{N*}a_N^*B\simeq B\otimes_kR\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted for the
frame-bundle projection $a_N:P_N\to B_N$; the comparison is used only on the
nerve and through the finite local models.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: build the free frame-space quotient, prove the fiber cohomology gap, and apply the bounded pullback comparison on the free-action nerve. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §3.1 (the Stiefel manifold of frames is an $n$-acyclic free manifold for a linear group, giving smooth resolutions) with §2.2.1-2.2.5 and §2.7.1-2.7.2 (limits over resolutions and the finite-resolution picture); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology §4.2 pp. 375-378 (fiber bundles over paracompact base spaces are fibrations, Theorem 4.41) for the fibration input to the Serre spectral sequence. Step 1 (frame space and quotient): nonvanishing pivot minors give graph charts and algebraic sections of $U_N\to B_N$, exhibiting $U_N\to B_N$ as a locally trivial principal $G$-bundle with an algebraic section over each chart; the action is free ([[def-free-group-action]], [[def-locally-trivial-fiber-bundle]]) and $X_N$ is the associated construction of [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]] with local charts $V\times X$. Step 2 (fiber cohomology gap): [[lem-general-linear-stiefel-frame-spaces-have-the-cohomology-gap]] supplies, by Gram-Schmidt and the cohomological Serre spectral sequence of the complex Stiefel sphere bundles, $H^0(U_N;k)=k$ and $H^j(U_N;k)=0$ for $1\le j\le r_N$. Step 3 (stabilization): pullback along the simplicial map $G^\bullet\times P_N\to G^\bullet\times X$ is levelwise a locally trivial bundle with fiber $U_N$, so the bounded pullback comparison of [[lem-locally-trivial-acyclic-fibers-give-bounded-derived-pullback-equivalences]] applies in every nerve degree with the finite models of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] and [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]]; locally split Cech descent ([[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]) identifies the equivariant Hom groups with Hom groups on $X_N$ in the stated range, gives the resolution-triple description of the image and retract closure, and shows independence of $N$ by applying the image criterion on products of resolutions where inverse comparisons are unique. No global splitting $Ra_{N*}a_N^*B=B\otimes R\Gamma(U_N;k)$ is asserted; the comparison is used only to bound the unit cone and test descent, so genuine characteristic-class transgressions are preserved. [AC as declared]

items.title: Cartesian simplicial sheaves model actual equivariant derived Hom
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The definition [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] gives a locally small triangulated category with conservative restriction to $X$ and the stated ordinary shift. Coinduced simplicial injectives compute its derived morphisms. Locally split free-action descent identifies its finite GL Stiefel resolution with the full bounded resolution-triple subcategory on $X_N$. The bounded Hom and image comparisons of [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] hold, including the degree-zero ring comparison and retract closure. The category is idempotent complete. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: build the ambient simplicial derived category, transport the Stiefel comparisons through locally split descent, and split idempotents by the telescope construction. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, Appendix B1-B6 (simplicial description of $D^b_G(X)$ and its triangulated equivalence with the Cartesian-cohomology subcategory) and §2.4.1-2.4.6, §2.5.1-2.5.4 (fibered-category description and triangulated structure); BBD §1.4.3 and §2.1.1-2.1.3 for the ordinary t-structure input. Step 1 (triangulated structure): Cartesian cohomology is preserved by truncation, shifts and cones because the nerve inverse images are exact and cohomology is computed by the long exact sequence; constructibility of the degree-zero restriction is closed under the same operations by [[lem-field-module-sheaves-have-injective-derived-models]] and [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]]; restriction to $X$ detects the zero object because Cartesian cohomology is determined in degree zero, and the Hom groups are set-sized because the ambient derived category has an injective model. Step 2 (Stiefel comparison): apply locally split Cech derived descent to the free Stiefel resolution $G^\bullet\times P_N\to X_N$; the unit-cone bound and image criterion of [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] give exactly the resolution triples and the bounded Hom comparison, and uniqueness of the comparisons supplies the coherence cocycles; the degree-zero comparison respects composition, hence is a ring comparison, and retract closure needs no degree-one extension-closure assumption. Step 3 (idempotents): for an idempotent $e$ on a bounded object $K$, form the telescope: let $S$ be the countable sum of copies of $K$ in the bounded-below derived category of all simplicial sheaves and let $T=\operatorname{Cone}(1-\operatorname{shift}(e):S\to S)$; exact coproducts give $H(T)=\operatorname{colim}(H(K),H(e))=\operatorname{im}H(e)$, so $T$ is bounded with Cartesian finite-rank constructible cohomology; the first-summand map $i:K\to T$ satisfies $ie=i$, the componentwise-$e$ map $S\to K$ gives $p:T\to K$ with $pi=e$, and $ip$ is an isomorphism, so replacing $p$ by $p(ip)^{-1}$ splits $e$ inside the category. This proves idempotent completeness without importing a Karoubi completion. No derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is claimed. [AC as declared]

items.title: Constructible six functors, proper base change and normalized equivariant duality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has characteristic zero, and that a product $G$ of complex general linear groups acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties. The coherent ordinary six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category $D^b_{G,c}$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] for equivariant algebraic maps: $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$, composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection formula and trace. For a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the actual exchange $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey Cartesian pasting. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. The normalized dualizing object restricts to the ordinary $\omega_X$; a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ has $\omega_X^G=k_X[2d]$. This is not the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift.
items.strategy: Assume AC; $k$ characteristic zero. Route: apply the ordinary coherent six operations at each finite free resolution, assemble them over the finite-resolution triples, and normalize the dualizing object by the Grassmannian resolution. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §3.1-3.6 (construction of the functors on smooth resolutions; tensor and Hom; $f^*,f^!,f_*,f_!$; their adjunctions, base change, composition and projection/trace properties; equivariant Verdier duality; equivariant constructible sheaves) and §1.9 with Appendix A (acyclicity enabling the resolution comparisons). Step 1 (operations): at each smooth free resolution use the ordinary constructed operations of [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] and [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]; smooth base-change comparison gives compatible transition isomorphisms, and the finite-resolution triples of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] assemble actual equivariant operations rather than unrelated isomorphisms. Adjunctions and the coherent projection/exchange/trace maps use the ordinary units and counits; their triangle and pasting identities hold at one sufficiently large finite resolution for all objects in the finite diagram and transfer through the fully faithful comparison, so Cartesian pasting and composition are preserved. Step 2 (normalization): at the Stiefel resolution $P_N\to X_N$ with base $B_N$ the normalized dualizing object is $\omega_{X_N}\otimes a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}$, correcting ordinary Verdier duality by $-2\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N$; its restriction to $X$ is the ordinary $\omega_X$, and complex orientation identifies it with $k[2\dim_{\mathbb C}X]$ when $X$ is smooth, with no group-dimension shift. Biduality, the two dual exchange identities, proper equality and the coherent unit/counit laws follow from the ordinary supplier [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]] together with the equivariant duality construction of the source. This is the unnormalized-quotient-stack shift exclusion recorded in the design. [AC as declared]

items.title: General linear Stiefel perverse normalization is exact and conservative
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the finite GL Stiefel resolution $P_N=U_N\times X\to X_N=P_N/G$ of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] for $G=\prod_i\operatorname{GL}_{n_i}(\mathbb C)$. Put $s_N=\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N$. The middle-perverse structure on the actual $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] is detected by restriction to $X$, and the functor $A\mapsto Q_N(A)[s_N]$ is perverse exact and conservative. Perverse truncations lift through sufficiently large bounded finite-resolution image comparisons. At the actual degree-zero Hom stabilization bound, lifted finite projectors preserve and reflect perverse concentration and simplicity after correcting the common shift $s_N$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Route: compute the dimension correction $s_N=u_N-g$ from the smooth projections, pull the ordinary perverse inequalities through the smooth t-exact functors of [[lem-smooth-complex-pullback-is-exact-for-the-middle-perverse-t-structure]], and lift truncations and finite projectors through the bounded image criterion. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §5.1 (equivariant perverse sheaves defined by the forgetful restriction; the quotient/induction equivalences) and §3.1 (complex Stiefel resolutions); BBD §2.1.1-2.1.3 and §2.1.9-2.1.15 (ordinary perverse t-structure and its behavior under smooth pullback and refinement). Step 1 (dimension correction): the projections $\operatorname{pr}_X:P_N\to X$ and $q_N:P_N\to X_N$ are smooth of complex relative dimensions $u_N$ and $g$, and $q_N^*Q_N(A)=\operatorname{pr}_X^*A_X$; since $s_N=u_N-g$, [[lem-smooth-complex-pullback-is-exact-for-the-middle-perverse-t-structure]] converts the perverse inequalities on $A_X$ into those on $Q_N(A)[s_N]$, and surjective pullback reflects them and zero objects. Step 2 (truncation lifting): apply ordinary perverse truncation to $Q_N(A)[s_N]$ and shift back; its principal-bundle pullback is $\operatorname{pr}_X^*({}^p\tau A_X)$, so it satisfies the finite-resolution image criterion of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] for all sufficiently large $N$; uniqueness of truncation gives resolution independence and t-exactness, and boundedness of the ordinary t-structure means one sufficiently large $N$ handles the finite collection of truncations and the finite diagram. Step 3 (projectors): the degree-zero ring comparison of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] lifts finite families of orthogonal idempotents; the telescope splitting of that lemma splits them inside $D^b_{G,c}$; perverse exactness and conservativity of the normalized functor reflect perverse concentration and simplicity of the lift after the common shift $s_N$ is corrected. No arbitrary perverse object on $X_N$ is asserted to descend, and no derived full faithfulness of restriction to $X$ is used. [AC as declared]

items.title: Middle perverse t structure glues and has simple intersection complexes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. On the equivariant constructible derived category $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], middle perversity is defined on smooth complex strata $S$ by $H^q(i_S^*A)=0$ for $q>-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$ and $H^q(i_S^!A)=0$ for $q<-\dim_{\mathbb C}S$; these inequalities give a bounded t-structure independent of compatible refinement and gluing across algebraic open/closed decompositions, and the equivariant structure is detected by restriction to $X$. Its heart is abelian of finite length, and its simple objects are the intermediate extensions $\operatorname{IC}_Z(L)=j_{!*}L[\dim_{\mathbb C}Z]$ of simple finite-rank local systems on dense smooth opens of irreducible supports, with equivariant data in the equivariant category. If $A,B$ lie in the heart, then $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B[m])=0$ for $m<0$. A simple object's endomorphism ring is a division $k$-algebra, not asserted to equal $k$.
items.strategy: Assume AC; $k$ of characteristic zero. Route: transport the ordinary middle-perverse core of [[thm-ordinary-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]] through the normalized finite-resolution bridge of [[lem-general-linear-stiefel-perverse-normalization-is-exact-and-conservative]], then repeat the recollement and intermediate-extension arguments inside the equivariant category using the six operations of [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]]. Sources: BBD §1.4.1-1.4.26 (recollement axioms 1.4.3; Theoreme 1.4.10 gluing the t-structure; Propositions 1.4.12-1.4.18; the intermediate extension 1.4.22 with its no-subobject/no-quotient characterization 1.4.24-1.4.25; Proposition 1.4.26 describing simple objects) and §2.1.1-2.1.23 (perverse t-structure on stratified spaces, Propositions 2.1.3/2.1.9/2.1.11, comparison 2.1.12-2.1.15, descent 2.1.19-2.1.23); Bernstein-Lunts Part I §5.1-5.2 (equivariant perverse heart, finite length, simples as equivariant IC sheaves). Step 1 (transfer): the ordinary core supplies the t-structure, duality exchange, intermediate extension, finite length and negative Hom on $D_c^b(X;k)$; the Stiefel-normalization bridge constructs the equivariant perverse structure with t-exact conservative restriction to $X$ and normalized finite-resolution comparison. Step 2 (heart and length): abelianness is the truncation kernel/cokernel argument; restriction to $X$ is exact and conservative on the heart, so a strictly increasing or decreasing subobject chain gives one in the finite-length ordinary heart; negative Hom is t-structure orthogonality in the equivariant derived category; a nonzero endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is invertible, giving a division algebra. Step 3 (IC classification): the equivariant six operations give the open/closed localization triangles and the intermediate-extension image construction; applying the ordinary recollement argument inside the equivariant t-structure shows the intermediate image has no boundary subobject or quotient, that a simple equivariant local system on a dense smooth open gives a simple intermediate extension, and that each simple heart object arises this way. Connected $G$ preserves the irreducible support components and the intrinsic local-system locus; degree-zero equivariant Hom is computed by the internal Hom adjunction and the simplicial augmentation, and on $G\times X$ the two descent pullbacks of a heart morphism agree at the identity and hence, $G$ being connected, on all degree-zero product sections; thus the forgetful heart functor is fully faithful on equivariant objects, consistent with the simple-local-system formulation. This is heart full faithfulness, not derived full faithfulness. [AC as declared]

items.title: Equivariant constructible Ext is degreewise finite and compatible with characteristic zero scalars
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be a product of complex general linear groups acting algebraically on a separated finite-type complex algebraic variety $X$, and let $k$ have characteristic zero. For bounded algebraically constructible $A,B$ in the actual $D^b_{G,c}(X;k)$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]], every $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ is finite-dimensional and vanishes for sufficiently negative $m$. For every characteristic-zero field extension $k\to K$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)\otimes_kK\to\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A_K,B_K)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $A$ and $B$ and compatible with shifts and Yoneda composition. Extension commutes with the coherent six operations, normalized Verdier duality, perverse truncation and intermediate extension on these bounded constructible objects. The total Ext space need not be finite-dimensional, and simplicity is not asserted to be preserved under extension.
items.strategy: Assume AC; $k$ of characteristic zero. Route: choose one sufficiently large finite Stiefel resolution, identify Ext with an ordinary Hom group of a finite-type variety, and use the finite constructible cochain models for finiteness and scalar extension; transfer the conclusion to the perverse structure through unique truncation triangles. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §2.7.2 and §3.1 (finite approximations and their interval bounds), §2.8 and §3.6 (constructibility and its preservation by the functors), §5.1 (equivariant perverse sheaves); BBD §2.1 for the ordinary perverse input. Step 1 (finiteness and vanishing): choose an interval $I$ containing $A$ and $B[m]$ and $N$ with $r_N\ge\operatorname{length}(I)$; [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]] identifies $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(A,B)$ with an ordinary Hom group on the finite-type variety $X_N$, which the finite cochain models of [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]] make finite-dimensional; if $A\le a$ and $B\ge b$ then $B[m]\ge b-m$, so the Hom group vanishes for $m<b-a$ by t-structure orthogonality. Step 2 (scalar extension): on the simplicial category extension of coefficients is termwise tensor with $K$ and commutes with inverse image and with free quotient descent, so $Q_N(A_K)=(A_N)_K$; the same $N$ works over both fields because the Stiefel cohomology vanishing is field-independent and the finite cochain models commute with coefficient extension; in the resulting commutative square of Hom comparisons the vertical arrows are the full-faithfulness isomorphisms, so the top horizontal arrow is an isomorphism. Composition is preserved because the comparisons are induced by functors, and one $N$ serves finitely many composable classes, giving Yoneda compatibility. This is a finite-stage proof; no infinite totalization or infinite product of injectives is tensored with $K$. Step 3 (operations and perverse structure): ordinary scalar comparison commutes with the coherent operations by [[thm-constructible-six-functors-proper-base-change-and-verdier-duality]] through their finite constructible models; the normalized perverse functor of [[lem-general-linear-stiefel-perverse-normalization-is-exact-and-conservative]] is exact and conservative, its truncation triangles extend uniquely, and extension is exact on the heart of [[thm-middle-perverse-t-structure-glues-and-has-simple-intersection-complexes]]; applying this to the perverse-degree-zero image defining the intermediate extension $j_{!*}$ proves intermediate-extension and IC commutation. Simplicity under extension is deliberately not asserted. [AC as declared]

items.title: Equivariant Ext of a point is degreewise finite and not total finite
items.statement: Let $G=\mathbb C^\times$ act trivially on the point $X=\operatorname{pt}$, with $k$ any characteristic-zero field, in the setting of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] ([[def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group]]). Then $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)$ is $k$ for nonnegative even $m$ and zero otherwise. Hence it is degreewise finite and its total direct sum is infinite-dimensional. Restriction to the ordinary point is not derived fully faithful.
items.strategy: Route: use the full-rank Stiefel approximation $U_N=\mathbb C^N\setminus\{0\}$ with quotient $B_N=\mathbb P^{N-1}$ and gap $r_N=2(N-1)$ from [[lem-product-general-linear-stiefel-approximations-stabilize-bounded-constructible-hom]]; for each fixed $m$ choose $N$ with $r_N\ge m$ and apply the bounded Hom comparison to get $\operatorname{Ext}_G^m(k,k)\cong H^m(\mathbb P^{N-1};k)$, computed, after identifying $\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^N)$ with $\mathbb P^{N-1}$ through its standard charts ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]]), from the standard cell structure as one cell in each even real degree $0,2,\dots,2(N-1)$ with zero differentials ([[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]], [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]). This identifies the value with $H^m(BG;k)$ as stated in [[thm-equivariant-constructible-ext-is-degreewise-finite-and-compatible-with-characteristic-zero-scalars]]; infinitely many even groups are nonzero, so the total direct sum is infinite-dimensional, while each degree is finite and the groups vanish for negative $m$. Ordinary Ext on a point vanishes in positive degrees, so the degree-two class also proves that restriction to the ordinary point is not derived fully faithful. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §2.7.2 (the classifying-space description of $D^b_G(\mathrm{pt})$ as complexes with locally constant cohomology on $BG$, constant for connected $G$) and §3.1 (Stiefel resolutions); Hatcher, Algebraic Topology Example 0.6 and §3.2 (cellular structure and cohomology of $\mathbb P^n$). The displayed computation is finite and choice-free apart from consuming the AC-assumed suppliers.
